line-pahacha-9.source: ନବମ ପାହାଚେ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ନବଗ୍ରହ / ଯୋଡ଼ହସ୍ତେ ଛନ୍ତି ଠିଆ ଚାହିଁ ତୁମ ମୁହଁ
line-pahacha-9.roman: nabama pāhāce dṛśya hele nabagraha / yoṛahaste chanti ṭhiā cāhiṁ tuma muhaṁ
line-pahacha-9.english: {0:On the ninth}{1: step,}{4: the nine planetary deities}{3: became}{2: visible;}{6: they are}{7: standing}{5: with folded hands,}{8: gazing upon}{9: your}{10: face.}

line-pahacha-16.source: ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ପାହାଚେ ମାତା ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଦେବୀଙ୍କୁ / ସ୍ମରିଲି ସୃଷ୍ଟିର ମୂଳ ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଶକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ

line-pahacha-19.source: ଉଣେଇଶ ପାହାଚରେ ପତିତପାବନ / ମନ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳ ଅତି ଲଭିବାକୁ ଦର୍ଶନ

line-pahacha-19.grammarNote: pāhācare is locative. patitapābana stands as the devotional focus. labhibāku is an infinitive of purpose in -bāku governing darśana.

line-pahacha-21.roman: eko'iśi pāhāce praṇāmī debadebī / ḍākili darśana di'a jagannātha swāmī

line-pahacha-21.grammarNote: praṇāmī is a non-finite conjunctive participle ('having saluted'). debadebī is a dvandva compound ('gods and goddesses'). ḍākili is 1st person past. di'a is a direct 2nd person imperative.

line-113.grammarNote: Sanskrit. 'śrī-sāīnāthacaraṇāmṛtapūtacittāstatpādasevanaratāḥ' contains two nom. pl. masc. compounds joined by sandhi: 'śrī-sāīnātha-caraṇāmṛta-pūta-cittāḥ' + 'tat-pāda-sevana-ratāḥ'; 'satataṃ' is adverb; 'bhaktyā' is instrumental singular feminine.

line-114.english: {4:having emerged }{3:from the flood }{2:of sins }{1:born }{0:of the cycle of worldly existence, }{5:they }{9:fully attain }{8:the supreme }{7:abode }{6:of absolute liberation.}

words.gloss: having emerged, escaped; vinirgatāḥ, nominative plural

line-114.grammarNote: Sanskrit. 'saṃsārajanyaduritaughavinirgatāste' is nom. pl. masc. compound 'vinirgatāḥ' + nom. pl. pronoun 'te'; 'kaivalyadhāma paramaṃ' is accusative singular neuter; 'samavāpnuvanti' is 3rd plural present active verb.

line-116.english: {3:surely becomes }{2:a vessel of grace }{0:of the Sadguru, }{1:Sāīnātha.}

words.gloss: of Sāīnātha; Sāī (“master” or “lord”) names the revered spiritual teacher Śirḍī Sāī Bābā here; nātha means “lord” or “protector”
a fit vessel and recipient of grace

line-116.grammarNote: Sanskrit. 'sadguroḥ' and 'sāīnāthasya' are genitive singular masculine; 'kṛpāpātraṃ' is nominative singular neuter compound; 'bhaveddhruvam' is sandhi: 3rd sing. optative 'bhavet' + adverb 'dhruvam'.

line-120.source: न दत्तगुरु साई मा मजवरी कधीही रुसो
line-120.roman: na Dattaguru Sāī mā majavarī kadhīhī ruso
line-120.english: {0:May}{1: Datta Guru}{2: Sāī,}{3: Mother,}{0,5: never}{6: be angry}{4: with me.}

words.gloss: Dattatreya the master; Datta means “given”; the name refers to Dattātreya, son of Atri and Anasūyā

line-120.grammarNote: Marathi 3rd person optative verb form 'ruso' with prohibitive/optative negative particle 'na'. 'majavarī' is 1st person singular pronoun 'maja' with postposition '-varī' (upon).

line-124.source: परी न गुरु साई मजवरी कधीही रुसो
line-124.roman: parī na guru sāī majavarī kadhīhī ruso
line-124.english: {0:Yet}{1: may}{2: Guru}{3: Sāī}{1,5: never}{6: be angry}{4: with me.}
line-124.grammarNote: 'parī' is a poetic adversative conjunction meaning 'yet' or 'however'. 'guru sāī' functions as the compound subject.

line-131.source: न दत्त गुरु साई मजवरी कधीही रुसो
line-131.roman: na datta guru sāī majavarī kadhīhī ruso
line-131.english: {0:May}{1: Datta}{2: Guru}{3: Sāī}{0,5: never}{6: be angry}{4: with me.}
line-131.grammarNote: 'datta guru sāī' forms the composite divine subject. 'majavarī' carries the postposition '-varī' (on/upon).

line-150.source: पदी प्रणय वोहरो निखिल दृश्य बाबा दिसो
line-150.roman: padī praṇaya voharo nikhila dṛśya bābā diso
line-150.english: {1:May deep love }{2:stream }{0:at the feet; }{3:may the entire }{4:visible world }{6:appear as }{5:Bābā.}
line-150.grammarNote: 'voharo' is 3rd person optative of archaic Marathi 'voharaṇe' (to stream/flow). 'diso' is optative of 'disaṇe' (to appear/be seen).

line-151.source: न दत्त गुरु साई मज उपरी या जनेला रुसो
line-151.roman: na datta guru sāī maja uparī yā janelā ruso
line-151.grammarNote: 'janelā' carries the dative/accusative marker '-lā' appended to 'jana' (person/humble servant). 'maja uparī' means 'upon me'.

line-160.source: श्री नारायण वासुदेवाय सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईनाथ महाराज की जय
line-160.roman: śrī nārāyaṇa vāsudevāya saccidānanda sadguru sāīnātha mahārāja kī jaya
line-160.english: {8:Victory}{7: to }{0:Holy }{1:Nārāyaṇa, }{2:unto Vāsudeva, }{4:the True Master, }{3:existence, consciousness, and bliss embodied, }{6:Great King }{5:Sāīnātha!}

words.gloss: Lord Viṣṇu; Nārāyaṇa is the refuge of living beings and rests upon the primordial waters
existence, consciousness, and bliss, describing the Guru himself
Lord Sāī / Sāīnātha; Sāī (“master” or “lord”) names the revered spiritual teacher Śirḍī Sāī Bābā here

line-160.grammarNote: Hybrid Sanskrit-Hindi acclamation formula: Sanskrit dative singular vāsudevāya alongside Hindi genitive postposition kī and noun jaya.

line-162.source: विहितमविहितं वा सर्वमेतत्क्षमस्व जय जय करुणाब्धे श्रीप्रभो साईनाथ ॥
line-162.roman: vihitamavihitaṁ vā sarvametatkṣamasva jaya jaya karuṇābdhe śrīprabho sāīnātha ||
line-162.english: {0:prescribed }{1:or unprescribed, }{2:or otherwise—}{5:forgive }{3:all }{4:this! }{6:Victory, }{7:victory, }{9:O ocean }{8:of compassion, }{10:O glorious }{11:Lord, }{12:O Sāīnātha!}

words.gloss: O Lord Sāī / Sāīnātha (vocative); Sāī (“master” or “lord”) names the revered spiritual teacher Śirḍī Sāī Bābā here

line-162.grammarNote: Internal sandhi: vihitam + avihitaṁ -> vihitamavihitaṁ; sarvam + etat + kṣamasva -> sarvametatkṣamasva. kṣamasva is 2nd sg. imperative ātmanepada of root kṣam. Vocative singulars: karuṇābdhe (from -i stem), śrīprabho (from -u stem), sāīnātha (from -a stem).

line-163.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईनाथ महाराज की जय

words.gloss: existence, consciousness, and bliss, describing the Guru himself

line-163.grammarNote: Standard Hindi devotional victory acclamation with Sanskrit compound epithets acting as a uninflected title string before the postposition kī.

line-164.english: {0:King of kings, }{1:King of yogis, }{2:supreme reality, }{4:Great King }{3:Sāīnātha!}

words.gloss: king among yogis / master of disciplines (yogi-rāja)

featureDispositions.reason: Sāī is called ocean of compassion while offenses are confessed.
He descends as Datta and is hailed as manifest supreme reality/Rāma incarnate.
The devotees attain the supreme abode of absolute liberation.
The speaker explicitly has no refuge other than Sāī’s lotus feet.
Service to foot-dust and sustained service at his feet are explicit.
All performed action is surrendered to Nārāyaṇa.
Meditation on the name and day-and-night contemplation are stated.
The Lord is asked to forgive and be gracious.
The worship-with-lights opening and royal closing acclamation name Sāī.
The sung acclamation addresses divine Guru Datta.
The meditation addresses the King among Gurus.
The worship-with-lights opening and royal closing acclamation name Sāī.

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय
line-01-jai.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-01-jai.grammarNote: Feminine genitive postposition kī agrees with feminine noun jaya in the conventional celebratory formula.

words.gloss: please take; please do (polite precative auxiliary)

line-03-sun-lije-arji.grammarNote: Compound verb suna līje combines main verb stem sun- with polite precative auxiliary lenā (līje); hamārī agrees in feminine singular with arajī.

line-07-daya-karo.source: दया करो दे दो बाबा कृपा की छाया
line-07-daya-karo.roman: Dayā karo de do bābā kṛpā kī chāyā
line-07-daya-karo.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative clauses: dayā karo and compound imperative de do; kī agrees in feminine singular with chāyā.

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.roman: Tukā kahe sevā merī bholī bhāvaḍī
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.grammarNote: Tukā kahe is the standard third-person singular signature formula; merī, bholī, and bhāvaḍī all agree in feminine singular with sevā.

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया
line-10-utho-panduranga.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga prabhāta samaya ā gayā

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-10-utho-panduranga.grammarNote: Uṭho is an imperative second-person plural/honorific; ā gayā is a compound verb (ā- + gayā) expressing completed arrival with masculine subject samaya.

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.source: वैष्णवों का मेला गरुड़ पार आ गया
line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.roman: Vaiṣṇavoṁ kā melā Garuḍa Pāra ā gayā

words.gloss: of Vaishnavas; of devotees of Vishnu

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.grammarNote: Garuḍa Pāra is an unmarked locative goal of motion; melā is masculine singular governing the compound verb ā gayā.

line-12-garuda-par-se.source: गरुड़ पार से महाद्वार देहरी तक
line-12-garuda-par-se.roman: Garuḍa Pāra se mahādvāra deharī taka
line-12-garuda-par-se.english: {2:From }{0:the Garuda }{1:platform }{5:up to }{4:the threshold }{3:of the main gate,}
line-12-garuda-par-se.grammarNote: Ablative se paired with inclusive postposition taka establishes a continuous spatial corridor between two temple landmarks.

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.source: शुक सनकादिक नारद तुम्बर भक्त हैं कोटि
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.roman: Śuka Sanakādika Nārada Tumbara bhakta haiṁ koṭi
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.english: {0:Shuka, }{1:Sanaka and the sages, }{2:Narada, }{3:Tumburu, }{6:and crores }{4:of devotees }{5:are present.}

words.gloss: the enlightened sage son of Vyasa

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.grammarNote: A list of proper nouns acting as plural subject governing the plural auxiliary haiṁ; koṭi functions as a post-nominal numeral quantifier modifying bhakta.

line-15-trishula-damaru.source: त्रिशूल डमरू लेकर आये गिरिजा के पति
line-15-trishula-damaru.roman: Triśūla ḍamarū lekara āye Girijā ke pati

words.gloss: small hourglass drum associated with Śiva

line-15-trishula-damaru.grammarNote: Lekara is a conjunctive participle ('having taken'); āye is plural/honorific masculine agreeing with the subject Girijā ke pati.

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.source: कलियुग का भक्त नामा बना कीर्तनी
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.roman: Kaliyuga kā bhakta Nāmā banā kīrtanī
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.english: {3:Nama, }{2:the devotee }{0,1:of the Kali age, }{4:has become }{5:the lead singer of praise,}

words.gloss: kirtan singer; lead performer of holy song

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.grammarNote: Kaliyuga kā bhakta modifies Nāmā in apposition; banā is a simple past/perfective verb governing predicate noun kīrtanī.

line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.source: पीठ पीछे खड़ी आके बन्दगी ये जनी
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.roman: Pīṭha pīche khaḍī āke bandagī ye Janī
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.english: {2:Standing }{0,1:right behind his back, }{5:this }{6:Jani }{3:has come }{4:in humble homage.}
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.grammarNote: Pīṭha pīche is a locative phrase; khaḍī is feminine singular agreeing with Janī; āke is a conjunctive participle.

line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.source: उठो उठो श्री साईंनाथ गुरु चरण कमल दिखलाओ
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.roman: Uṭho uṭho Śrī Sāīnātha guru caraṇa kamala dikhalāo
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative uṭho uṭho shows heightened urgency; caraṇa kamala is a karmadhāraya compound functioning as direct object of causative imperative dikhalāo.

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.source: फिर भी अज्ञान सी छाई है तुम्हरी योग माया
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.roman: Phira bhī ajñāna sī chāī hai tumharī yoga māyā
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.grammarNote: Compound phrase 'yoga māyā' acts as the feminine singular subject agreeing with 'chāī hai'; 'ajñāna sī' is an adjectival modifier of state.

line-24-bho-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative structure: 'Bho' introduces the titles; 'bhavatimiranāśaka' is a Sanskrit tatpuruṣa compound (bhava + timira + nāśaka) modifying 'ravi'.

line-32-uthakar-netra.source: उठाकर नेत्र पलकें दीन बन्धु रमाकान्ता
line-32-uthakar-netra.roman: Uṭhākara netra palakeṁ dīna bandhu Ramākāntā
line-32-uthakar-netra.english: {0:Lifting }{2:the eyelids }{1:of Your eyes, }{4:O friend }{3:of the humble, }{5:O beloved of Lakshmi,}

words.gloss: beloved of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī, as fortune and splendour; Lord Viṣṇu

line-32-uthakar-netra.grammarNote: 'uṭhākara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on 'dekho' in line 33; 'dīna bandhu' and 'Ramākāntā' are vocative epithets.

line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.source: सुनाओ मधुर वाणी हरो ताप साईंनाथा
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.roman: Sunāo madhura vāṇī haro tāpa Sāīnāthā
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative verbs 'sunāo' and 'haro' addressed to the vocative 'Sāīnāthā'.

line-36-sahan-karke-aao.source: सहन करके आओ चाहे भेट कृष्ण देवा
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.roman: Sahana karake āo cāhe bheṭa Kṛṣṇa devā
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.english: {0,1:bearing it patiently, }{2:come forth; }{3:one longs for }{4:a meeting, }{6:O Lord }{5:Krishna!}
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.grammarNote: 'sahana karake' is a conjunctive participle modifying 'āo'; 'cāhe bheṭa' has an inverted word order with implied subject ('the world/devotee desires a meeting').

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग अब तो दर्शन दो सबको
line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga aba to darśana do sabako

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.grammarNote: Coordinate imperatives 'uṭho' and 'do'; 'Pāṇḍuraṅga' is vocative; 'to' adds emphatic pleading.

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.source: राई रखुमाबाई मन में आने दो दया
line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.roman: Rāī Rakhumābaī mana meṁ āne do dayā

words.gloss: Rakhumābāī, Rukmiṇī the gold-adorned goddess; consort of Viṭṭhala

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.grammarNote: Vocative direct address 'Rāī Rakhumābaī' governing permissive verbal construction 'āne do' with direct object 'dayā'.

words.gloss: Hanumān, the one with prominent jaws; Rāma’s divine attendant and devotee

line-45-garuda-hanumanta-thade.grammarNote: Plural subject 'Garuḍa Hanumanta' takes the stative participle 'ṭhāḍe' and imperfective verb 'johate'; 'bāṭa' is the accusative complement of the idiom.

line-48-vishnudasa-nama-khada.grammarNote: Appositive proper noun 'Viṣṇudāsa Nāmā' is the subject of the predicate adjective 'khaḍā' with conjunctive participle phrase 'lekara kākaḍā'.

line-49-lekar-pancharati.source: लेकर पञ्चारती करूँ बाबा की आरती
line-49-lekar-pancharati.roman: Lekara pañcāratī karūṁ bābā kī āratī
line-49-lekar-pancharati.english: {0:Holding }{1:the five-flame lamp, }{2:I offer }{5:worship with lights }{3,4:to Baba.}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-49-lekar-pancharati.grammarNote: First person singular verb 'karūṁ' taking 'āratī' as direct object; 'pañcāratī' is governed by 'lekara'.

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.source: उठो उठो हे बान्धव मनाओ ये रमाधव
line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.roman: Uṭho uṭho he bāndhava manāo ye Ramādhava

line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.english: {0:Krishnanatha }{6:fixes }{5:his consciousness }{3,4:at the feet }{1,2:of Datta Sai, }{7:O Sai.}

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.source: साईंनाथ के भक्ति ताप से उसको जलाया

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.grammarNote: Causative/transitive past verb 'jalāyā' taking pronoun 'usako' as direct object; 'bhakti tāpa se' is the instrumental cause.

line-61-aise-datta-deva.source: ऐसे दत्त देव शिरडी रहकर भी मिलते

line-61-aise-datta-deva.english: {0:In such a way} {1,2:Lord Datta} {6:meets seekers,} {4,5:even while dwelling} {3:in Shirdi.}

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.source: सगुण दर्शन पाने जन जन शिरडी आ रहा

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-72-arati-utaru-mere.grammarNote: Paṇḍharīnāthā is in the vocative case (Paṇḍharīnātha + ā extension common in devotional Marathi/Hindi verse).

line-80-inta-para-khada.source: ईंट पर खड़ा हुआ है सुन्दर बाबा

line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.source: उठकर भोर में बाबा खड़े हैं ईंट पे

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.source: केशवराज ईंट पे खड़े नामा चरण पूजते

words.gloss: King Keśava, the fine-haired lord, here Viṭṭhala

line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.source: साईंनाथ गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.source: दत्तराज गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.roman: Dattarāja guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया

verse-2.source:
तुम संसार शक्ति लय कीना । पालन हेतु अन्न धन दीना ॥
अन्नपूर्णा हुई जग पाला । तुम ही आदि सुन्दरी बाला ॥
प्रलयकाल सब नाशन हारी । तुम गौरी शिव शंकर प्यारी ॥
शिव योगी तुम्हरे गुण गावें । ब्रह्मा विष्णु तुम्हें नित ध्यावें ॥

śiva yōgī tumharē guṇa gāvēm̐ | brahmā viṣṇu tumhēṁ nita dhyāvēm̐ ||

verse-3.source:
रूप सरस्वती को तुम धारा । दे सुबुद्धि ऋषि मुनिन उबारा ॥
धर्यो रूप नरसिंह को अम्बा । परगट भई फाड़कर खम्बा ॥
रक्षा करि प्रह्लाद बचायो । हिरणाकुश को स्वर्ग पठायो ॥
लक्ष्मी रूप धरो जग माहीं । श्री नारायण अंग समाहीं ॥

rakṣā kari prahlāda bacāyō | hiraṇākuśa kō svarga paṭhāyō ||

verse-5.source:
केहरि वाहन सोह भवानी । लांगुर वीर चलत अगवानी ॥
कर में खप्पर खड्ग विराजै । जाको देख काल डर भाजै ॥
सोहै अस्त्र और त्रिशूला । जाते उठत शत्रु हिय शूला ॥
नगरकोटि में तुम्हीं विराजत । तिहूँ लोक में डंका बाजत ॥

sōhai astra aura triśūlā | jātē uṭhata śatru hiya śūlā ||
nagarakōṭi mēṁ tumhīṁ virājata | tihūm̐ lōka mēṁ ḍaṅkā bājata ||

verse-8.source:
जोगी सुर मुनि कहत पुकारी । योग न हो बिन शक्ति तुम्हारी ॥
शंकर आचारज तप कीनो । काम अरु क्रोध जीति सब लीनो ॥
निशिदिन ध्यान धरो शंकर को । काहू काल नहिं सुमिरो तुमको ॥
शक्ति रूप को मरम न पायो । शक्ति गई तब मन पछतायो ॥

niśidina dhyāna dharō śaṅkara kō | kāhū kāla nahiṁ sumirō tumakō ||

verse-10.source:
शत्रु नाश कीजै महारानी । सुमिरौं इकचित तुम्हें भवानी ॥
करो कृपा हे मातु दयाला । ऋद्धि सिद्धि दै करहु निहाला ॥
जब लगि जिओं दया फल पाऊँ । तुम्हरो यश मैं सदा सुनाऊँ ॥
दुर्गा चालीसा जो गावै । सब सुख भोग परम पद पावै ॥
देवीदास शरण निज जानी । करहु कृपा जगदम्ब भवानी ॥

The repeated nalla predicates their goodness; aṭiyā + ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku (for the devotees).

v4-l1.source: மதிநுதன் மங்கையோடு வடாலிருந்து மறையோதும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v4-l1.roman: matinutaṉ maṅkaiyōṭu vaṭāliruntu maṟaiyōtum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v4-l1.english: {4:Our}{5: Supreme Lord who,}{2: seated beneath the banyan tree}{0: with the moon-browed}{1: maiden,}{3: expounds the Vedas,}
v4-l1.grammarNote: matinutaṉ = mati (moon) + nutal (forehead, with euphonic nasalization); vaṭāliruntu = vaṭa (north/banyan) + āl (banyan tree) + iruntu (having stayed/sat); maṟaiyōtum = maṟai + ōtum (relative participle).

v4-l2.source: நதியொடு கொன்றைமாலை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v4-l2.roman: natiyoṭu koṉṟaimālai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v4-l2.english: {3:having adorned}{2: His crown with}{0: the river}{1: and a garland of golden shower blossoms,}{5: entered}{3: into my}{4: heart;}{6: therefore,}
v4-l2.grammarNote: natiyoṭu (nati + oṭu); muṭimēl split across sandhi as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ).

v4-l3.source: கொதியுறு காலன் அங்கி நமனோடு தூதர் கொடுநோய்க ளான பலவும்
v4-l3.roman: kotiyuṟu kālaṉ aṅki namaṉōṭu tūtar koṭunōyka ḷāṉa palavum
v4-l3.english: {0:wrathful}{1: Death,}{2: fire,}{3: Yama along with his}{4: messengers,}{6,7: and all the many}{5: severe afflictions}
v4-l3.grammarNote: kotiyuṟu = koti (boil/rage) + uṟu; namaṉōṭu (namaṉ + oṭu); koṭunōykaḷ split across sandhi as koṭunōyka + ḷāṉa (ḷ + āṉa).

v4-l4.source: அதிகுணம் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v4-l4.roman: atikuṇam nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v4-l4.english: {0:are supremely beneficial,}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v4-l4.grammarNote: atikuṇam = ati (supreme/exceeding) + kuṇam (guṇa / beneficial quality); sandhi split aṭiyā + ravarkku.

v5-l1.source: நஞ்சணி கண்டன் எந்தை மடவாள் தனோடும் விடையேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v5-l1.roman: nañjaṇi kaṇṭaṉ entai maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum viṭaiyēṟum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v5-l1.english: {2:Our Father}{6,7: and Supreme Lord,}{1: whose throat}{0: is adorned with poison,}{5: who mounts the bull}{4: along with}{3: the gentle maiden,}
v5-l1.grammarNote: nañjaṇi = nañju + aṇi; entai = eṉ + tantai (my/our father); maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum (maṭavāḷ + taṉ + oṭu + um); viṭaiyēṟum = viṭai + ēṟum (relative participle).

v5-l2.source: துஞ்சிருள் வன்னி கொன்றை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v5-l2.roman: tuñjiruḷ vaṉṉi koṉṟai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v5-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{1: Indian mesquite}{2: and golden shower blossoms,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: heart}{0: in the darkness of sleep;}{7: therefore,}

words.gloss: the darkness of sleep; here the time of His entry

v5-l2.grammarNote: tuñjiruḷ combines tuñcu (sleep) and iruḷ (darkness), read here as the time of His entry into the heart. Another possible construction relates abiding darkness to the adjacent tree; tuñcu can mean both sleep and abide. muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v5-l3.source: வெஞ்சின அவுணரோடும் உருமிடியும் மின்னும் மிகையான பூதமவையும்
v5-l3.roman: veñciṉa avuṇarōṭum urumiṭiyum miṉṉum mikaiyāṉa pūtamavaiyum

words.gloss: those elemental spirits / beings as well

v5-l3.grammarNote: avuṇarōṭum contains associative suffix -ōṭu and connective -um; urumiṭiyum, miṉṉum, and pūtamavaiyum have coordinating conjunctive -um; pūtamavaiyum combines pūtam + avai + um.

v5-l4.source: அஞ்சிடும் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v5-l4.roman: añciṭum nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē

words.gloss: will be filled with dread / will fear

v5-l4.grammarNote: añciṭum is future/habitual 3rd person neuter plural verb; aṭiyā ravarkku represents sandhi split of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); nalla nalla is an aṭukku-t-toṭar (intensive reduplication).

v6-l1.source: வாள்வரி யதளதாடை வரி கோவணத்தர் மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v6-l1.roman: vāḷvari yataḷatāṭai vari kōvaṇattar maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v6-l1.english: {0:Clad in radiant-striped }{1:skin as His garment, }{3:the wearer of a }{2:bound }{3:loincloth, }{6:united together }{5:with }{4:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: skin of that as His garment
the one who wears a loincloth

v6-l1.grammarNote: yataḷatāṭai contains glide y + ataḷatu (skin) + āṭai (garment); kōvaṇattar is a pronominal noun (3rd person honorific masculine); taṉōṭum contains reflexive singular taṉ + associative ōṭu + connective um.

v6-l2.source: நாண்மலர் வன்னி கொன்றை நதிசூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v6-l2.roman: nāṇmalar vaṉṉi koṉṟai naticūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v6-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:fresh blossoms, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:golden shower, }{3:and the river, }{4:came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v6-l2.grammarNote: nāṇmalar is sandhi of nāḷ (fresh/day) + malar (flower); vanteṉ is vantu (verbal participle) + eṉ (oblique 1st person singular 'my'); ataṉāl is instrumental ablative causal connective ('on account of that').

v6-l3.source: கோளரி யுழுவையோடு கொலையானை கேழல் கொடுநாக மோடு கரடி
v6-l3.roman: kōḷari yuḻuvaiyōṭu kolaiyāṉai kēḻal koṭunāka mōṭu karaṭi
v6-l3.english: {0:the predatory lion }{1:along with the tiger, }{2:the murderous elephant, }{3:the wild boar, }{5:along with }{4:the deadly serpent, }{6:and the bear,}
v6-l3.grammarNote: yuḻuvaiyōṭu includes inserted glide y and associative suffix -ōṭu; mōṭu represents sandhi of -m (from koṭunākam) + ōṭu.

v6-l4.source: ஆளரி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v6-l4.roman: āḷari nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v6-l4.grammarNote: aṭiyā ravarkku is the split surface form of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); avai is 3rd person neuter plural pronoun standing for all wild animals.

v7-l1.source: செப்பிள முலைநன்மங்கை ஒருபாக மாக விடையேறு செல்வனடைவார்
v7-l1.roman: ceppiḷa mulaiṉaṉmaṅkai orupāka māka viṭaiyēṟu celvaṉaṭaivār
v7-l1.english: With the {3:noble maiden }of {1:youthful }{0:cup-like }{2:breasts }{6:as }{4:one }{5:half, }{9:the prosperous Lord }{8:who mounts }{7:the bull}{10:—reached by}

words.gloss: reaching or settling upon Him (continuing with the waters in the next line)

v7-l1.grammarNote: The surface celvaṉaṭaivār spans celvaṉ and aṭaivu ār. The latter continues into the following line and describes the waters reaching or settling upon the Lord; it does not introduce devotees as an agent. The cup-like youthful breasts belong to the noble maiden, who is His half.

v7-l2.source: ஒப்பிள மதியும் அப்பும் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v7-l2.roman: oppiḷa matiyum appum muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v7-l2.english: {2:the waters—}{4:wearing them, }with the {0:peerless young }{1:moon, }{3:upon His crown, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v7-l2.grammarNote: oppiḷa = oppu (comparison/equal) + il (without) + a / iḷa (young); muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl (locative 'upon the crown') + aṇintu (adorned) + eṉ (my).

v7-l3.source: வெப்பொடு குளிரும் வாதம் மிகையான பித்தும் வினையான வந்து நலியா
v7-l3.roman: veppoṭu kuḷirum vātam mikaiyāṉa pittum viṉaiyāṉa vantu naliyā
v7-l3.english: {0:fever along with }{1:chills, }{2:wind-humor afflictions, }{3:excessive }{4:bile-humor afflictions, }{5:and distresses born of deeds }{7:will not }{6:come }{7:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: those born of past deeds / karmic distresses
will not afflict; will not cause harm

v7-l3.grammarNote: naliyā is a negative 3rd person neuter plural verb from root nali (to torment/crush); viṉaiyāṉa is an adjectival/pronominal appellative form referring to deeds/consequences.

v7-l4.source: அப்படி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v7-l4.roman: appaṭi nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v7-l4.english: {0:thus they are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v7-l4.grammarNote: appaṭi functions as an adverbial connective of manner ('just so / likewise'); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v8-l1.source: வேள்பட விழிசெய் தன்று விடைமே லிருந்து மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v8-l1.roman: vēḷpaṭa viḻicey taṉṟu viṭaimē liruntu maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v8-l1.english: {1:Having opened His eye }{2:on that day }{0:so that Kāma would perish, }{4:seated }{3:upon the bull }{7:together }{6:with }{5:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: for Kāma (the god of desire) to perish / fall

v8-l1.grammarNote: vēḷpaṭa is an infinitive of purpose/result (vēḷ + paṭa); viḻiceytaṉṟu is split into viḻicey + taṉṟu (ta- inserted before aṉṟu); viṭaimē liruntu is sandhi of viṭaimēl + iruntu.

v8-l2.source: வாண்மதி வன்னி கொன்றை மலர்சூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v8-l2.roman: vāṇmati vaṉṉi koṉṟai malarcūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v8-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:the radiant moon, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:and golden shower }{3:blossoms, }{4:He came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v8-l2.grammarNote: vāṇmati combines vāḷ (bright) + mati (moon); malarcūṭi is compound of malar (flower) + cūṭi (verbal participle 'having worn').

v8-l3.source: ஏழ்கடல் சூழிலங்கை அரையன்த னோடும் இடரான வந்து நலியா
v8-l3.roman: ēḻkaṭal cūḻilaṅkai araiyaṉta ṉōṭum iṭarāṉa vantu naliyā
v8-l3.english: {2:the king }{1:of Laṅkā }{1:surrounded by }{0:seven oceans }{3:along with }{4:all distresses }{6:will not }{5:come }{6:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: will not afflict; will not cause harm

v8-l3.grammarNote: ēḻkaṭal combines ēḻu (seven) + kaṭal (sea); araiyanta ṉōṭum represents araiyan (king) + oblique -ta- + associative -ōṭu + connective -um.

v8-l4.source: ஆழ்கடல் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v8-l4.roman: āḻkaṭal nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v8-l4.grammarNote: āḻkaṭal is a viṉait-tokai compound from āḻ (to sink/be deep) + kaṭal (ocean); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-l1.source: பலபல வேட மாகும் பரனாரி பாகன் பசுவேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v9-l1.roman: palapala vēṭa mākum paraṉāri pākaṉ pacuvēṟum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v9-l1.english: {3:The Supreme One,}{2: assuming}{0: manifold}{1: guises,}{4: having}{3: the woman}{4: as His half,}{6: our}{7: Supreme Lord}{5: who rides the bull,}

words.gloss: the Supreme One; the woman (in nāri-pākaṉ, woman-as-half)
one who has as His half

v9-l1.grammarNote: palapala is intensive reduplication of pala (many); vēṭa mākum combines vēṭam + ākum (relative participle); pacuvēṟum is pacu (bull) + ēṟum (mounting).

v9-l2.source: சலமக ளோடு எருக்கு முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v9-l2.roman: calamaka ḷōṭu erukku muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v9-l2.english: {4:wearing }{3:upon His crown }{0:the daughter of the waters }{1:along with }{2:crown flowers, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v9-l2.grammarNote: calamaka ḷōṭu represents calamakaḷ (calam 'water' + makaḷ 'daughter') + associative suffix -ōṭu; muṭimē laṇinteṉ is sandhi for muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v9-l3.source: மலர்மிசை யோனும் மாலும் மறையோடு தேவர் வருகால மான பலவும்
v9-l3.roman: malarmicai yōṉum mālum maṟaiyōṭu tēvar varukāla māṉa palavum
v9-l3.english: {1:He }{0:upon the lotus }{1:and }{2:Viṣṇu, }{3:along with }{3:the Vedas, }{4:the gods, }{7:and all the manifold things }{6:that constitute }{5:the future,}

words.gloss: Māl, the Great One, Viṣṇu, also
all the manifold entities as well

v9-l3.grammarNote: malarmicai yōṉum is sandhi for malarmicaiyōṉ (pronominal noun: 'he who is on the flower', Brahmā) + -um; mālum has connective -um; varukāla māṉa combines varukālam + āṉa.

v9-l4.source: அலைகடல் மேரு நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-l4.roman: alaikaṭal mēru nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-l4.grammarNote: alaikaṭal is a viṉait-tokai (alai 'surge/wave' + kaṭal 'sea'); aṭiyā ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees, }they are {8:good, }{9:good—}{7:exceedingly so; }{10,11:for His devotees—}{12:exceedingly so!}
v9-extra.grammarNote: Consists of three repeated cycles of the refrain formula aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla.

v10-l1.source: கொத்தலர் குழலி யோடு விசயற்கு நல்கு குணமாய வேட விகிர்தன்
v10-l1.roman: kottalar kuḻali yōṭu vicayaṟku nalku kuṇamāya vēṭa vikirtaṉ
v10-l1.english: {2:Along with }{1:Her of }{0:blossoming flower-cluster }{1:tresses, }{7:the Transcendent Lord of varied forms }who in {5:gracious }{6:hunter }{6:guise }{4:bestowed grace }{3:upon Arjuna,}

words.gloss: the Transcendent Lord of varied forms

v10-l1.grammarNote: kottalar is kottu (cluster) + alar (blossom); kuḻali yōṭu has inserted glide y and associative -ōṭu; vicayaṟku is dative singular of vicayaṉ (Arjuna); vikirtaṉ is derived from Sanskrit vikṛta ('one who assumes varied forms / the Transcendent').

v10-l2.source: மத்தமும் மதியும் நாகம் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v10-l2.roman: mattamum matiyum nākam muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v10-l2.english: {4:wearing}{0: datura,}{1: the crescent moon,}{2: and the serpent}{3: upon His crest,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: very heart;}{7: therefore,}
v10-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi breaks across tokens: `muṭi mēl` + `aṇintu` + `eṉ` yields surface tokens `muṭimē` and `laṇinteṉ`. Relative participle `pukunta` modifies causal instrumental pronoun `ataṉāl`. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v10-l3.source: புத்தரொ டமணை வாதில் அழிவிக்கும் அண்ணல் திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே
v10-l3.roman: puttaro ṭamaṇai vātil aḻivikkum aṇṇal tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē
v10-l3.english: {4:the exalted Lord’s }{5:sacred ash }{3:defeats }{0:Buddhists }{1:and Jains }{2:in debate—}{6:its goodness }{7:is assured; }{8:the sacred ash’s }{9:goodness }{10:is assured; }{11:the sacred ash’s }{12:goodness }{13:is assured.}

words.gloss: causes defeat; here, the sacred ash defeats opponents in debate

v10-l3.grammarNote: Aḻivikkum is a causative relative form attached to the full noun phrase aṇṇal tirunīṟu: the Lord’s sacred ash is the effective subject. Cemmai is its goodness or excellence; tiṭamē affirms that this is assured. The three performed occurrences are retained individually.

v10-l4.source: அத்தகு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-l4.roman: attaku nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-l4.english: {0:Such things are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v10-l4.grammarNote: Reduplication of `nalla` emphasizes absolute auspiciousness. Sandhi split across tokens: `aṭiyār` + `avarkku` -> `aṭiyā` and `ravarkku`.

v10-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees—}{7:exceedingly so; }{8,9:for His devotees—}{10:exceedingly so!}
v10-extra.grammarNote: Liturgical refrain repeating the cadence of the verse's final quarter (`aṭiyāravarkku mikavē`).

v11-l1.source: தேனமர் பொழில்கொள் ஆலை விளைசெந்நெல் துன்னி வளர்செம்பொன் எங்கும் நிகழ
v11-l1.roman: tēṉamar poḻilkoḷ ālai viḷaicennel tuṉṉi vaḷarcempoṉ eṅkum nikaḻa
v11-l1.english: Amid {0:honey-rich }{1:groves, }{2:sugarcane mills, }and {3:ripening red rice }{4:clustered together, }{5:fine gold abounding }{6:everywhere }{7:in sight,}
v11-l1.grammarNote: Infinitive `nikaḻa` functions adverbially/circumstantially ('as ... shines/manifests'). Compound chain: `tēṉ-amar` (honey-settling), `poḻil-koḷ` (grove-bearing), `viḷai-cem-nel` (ripening-red-paddy), `vaḷar-cem-poṉ` (growing-fine-gold).

v11-l2.source: நான்முகன் ஆதி யாய பிரமா புரத்து மறைஞான ஞான முனிவன்
v11-l2.roman: nāṉmukaṉ āti yāya piramā purattu maṟaiñāṉa ñāṉa muṉivaṉ
v11-l2.english: {6:the wise }{7:sage, }{5:versed in Vedic knowledge, }{3,4:of Brahmapuram, }{1,2:which takes its name from }{0:the Four-faced One,}

words.gloss: origin or beginning; here, the origin of the city’s name
being or becoming; linking the origin to Brahmapuram

v11-l2.grammarNote: Nāṉmukaṉ is the Four-faced One. Āti yāya relates the origin of Brahmapuram to him; it does not say that he owns the city. Maṟaiñāṉa gives Vedic knowledge, and ñāṉa qualifies the sage as wise. The English subject is this sage, continued by spoke in the next row.

v11-l3.source: தானுறு கோளும் நாளும் அடியாரை வந்து நலியாத வண்ணம் உரைசெய்
v11-l3.roman: tāṉuṟu kōḷum nāḷum aṭiyārai vantu naliyāta vaṇṇam uraicey
v11-l3.english: {7:spoke }{6:so that }{1:planets }{2:and asterisms, }{0:as they take their course, }{5:may not }{4:come }{5:and afflict }{3:devotees.}

words.gloss: spoke or composed; here, the sage’s utterance that forms the following word-garland

v11-l3.grammarNote: Naliyāta is negative and qualifies vaṇṇam: so that they do not afflict. Uraicey is the utterance/composition expression linked to the following garland of words; do not assert an overt past-tense suffix absent from the supplied form. English uses spoke as a finite clause, then resumes the resulting garland with this in the next sentence.

v11-l4.source: ஆனசொல் மாலை யோதும் அடியார்கள் வானில் அரசாள்வர் ஆணை நமதே
v11-l4.roman: āṉacol mālai yōtum aṭiyārkaḷ vāṉil aracāḷvar āṇai namatē
v11-l4.english: {3:Devotees }{2:who recite }{1:this garland }{0:of potent words }{5:shall reign }{4:in heaven; }{7:this is our }{6:solemn decree!}
v11-l4.grammarNote: Sandhi: `mālai` + `ōtum` -> `mālai yōtum`. Future verb `aracāḷvar` asserts the promised fruit. `āṇai namatē` is an emphatic nominal sentence of sovereign declaration.

v11-closing.grammarNote: Nominal sentence `āṇai namatē` (noun + possessive pronoun with emphatic `-ē`) chanted in fourfold repetition.

words.gloss: sacred little hall of consciousness at Chidambaram

invocation-tiruchitrambalam.grammarNote: Compound proper noun / holy acclamation: tiru (sacred) + ciṟu (subtle/little) + ampalam (hall/open space).

v1-l1.source: வேயுறு தோளி பங்கன் விடமுண்ட கண்டன் மிகநல்ல வீணை தடவி
v1-l1.roman: vēyuṟu tōḷi paṅkaṉ viṭamuṇṭa kaṇṭaṉ mikanalla vīṇai taṭavi
v1-l1.english: {2:He who has as His half}{1: the woman whose shoulders}{0: resemble bamboo,}{3,4: the One whose throat swallowed poison,}{7: strumming}{5: the exceedingly sweet}{6: lute,}

words.gloss: He who shares His half with

v1-l1.grammarNote: Participial clause: vēyuṟu (vēy + uṟu), tōḷi (fem. noun), paṅkaṉ (masc. appellative noun), viṭam-uṇṭa (relative participle), kaṇṭaṉ (appellative), taṭavi (adverbial participle).

v1-l2.source: மாசறு திங்கள் கங்கை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v1-l2.roman: mācaṟu tiṅkaḷ kaṅkai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v1-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{0: the spotless}{1: moon}{2: and Gaṅgā,}{6: entered}{4: into my}{5: heart;}{7: therefore,}
v1-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi splitting across whitespace tokens: muṭimēl split as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ). Causal postposition ataṉāl links this entry to the following consequences within the stanza. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v1-l3.source: ஞாயிறு திங்கள் செவ்வாய் புதன் வியாழன் வெள்ளி சனி பாம்பிரண்டும் உடனே
v1-l3.roman: ñāyiṟu tiṅkaḷ cevvāy putaṉ viyāḻaṉ veḷḷi caṉi pāmpiraṇṭum uṭaṉē
v1-l3.english: {0:Sun,}{1: Moon,}{2: Mars,}{3: Mercury,}{4: Jupiter,}{5: Venus,}{6: Saturn,}{7: and both serpents}{8: together}
v1-l3.grammarNote: List of planetary deities ending in pāmpiraṇṭum (pāmpu + iraṇṭu + um) and adverbial clitic uṭaṉē.

v1-l4.source: ஆசறு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v1-l4.roman: ācaṟu nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v1-l4.english: {0:are free of harm,}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v1-l4.grammarNote: Reduplicated adjectives nalla nalla for superlative emphasis. Sandhi split across whitespace: aṭiyā + ravarkku (aṭiyār + avarkku, dative plural).

v2-l1.source: என்பொடு கொம்பொடாமை இவை மார்பிலங்க எருதேறி ஏழையுடனே
v2-l1.roman: eṉpoṭu kompoṭāmai ivai mārpilaṅka erutēṟi ēḻaiyuṭaṉē
v2-l1.english: {0:With bones,}{1: tusk, and tortoise shell,}{2: these}{3: shining upon His chest,}{4: riding the bull}{5: together with the delicate maiden,}
v2-l1.grammarNote: kompoṭāmai = kompu + oṭu + āmai; mārpilaṅka = mārpu + ilaṅka (infinitive used adverbially); erutēṟi = erutu + ēṟi (adverbial participle).

v2-l2.source: பொன்பொதி மத்தமாலை புனல்சூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v2-l2.roman: poṉpoti mattamālai puṉalcūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v2-l2.english: {2:wearing}{1: a garland of datura flowers}{0: with gold within}{2: and the waters,}{3: He came}{5: and entered}{3: into my}{4: heart;}{6: therefore,}

words.gloss: containing gold; said of the flowers’ golden interiors

v2-l2.grammarNote: poṉpoti combines poṉ (gold) and poti (contain, enclose), describing the datura flowers. The image is gold within the flowers; pollen is not named. puṉalcūṭi = puṉal + cūṭi; vanteṉ = vantu + eṉ. The final causal phrase links to the following stanza predicate. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v2-l3.source: ஒன்பதொ டொன்றொடேழு பதினெட்டொடாறும் உடனாய நாள்க ளவைதாம்
v2-l3.roman: oṉpato ṭoṉṟoṭēḻu patiṉeṭṭoṭāṟum uṭaṉāya nāḷka ḷavaitām
v2-l3.english: {7:those}{6: asterisms}{7: themselves—}{0:the ninth,}{1: the tenth}{2: and sixteenth,}{3: the eighteenth}{4: and sixth,}{5: and those associated with them—}

words.gloss: the ninth asterism, with the following numbered ones
one: nine plus one, the tenth asterism (oṉṟu + oṭu, “with”)
seven: nine plus seven, the sixteenth asterism (ēḻu)
those accompanying or associated with them
those themselves; initial ḷ completes the preceding plural noun

v2-l3.grammarNote: The numeral construction names stellar positions, rather than a total: nine, nine plus one, nine plus seven, eighteen and six. The base nine is understood again with one and seven. uṭaṉāya describes the associated ones. nāḷkaḷ is split across nāḷka + ḷavaitām, the latter continuing with avai + tām (those themselves). The following row supplies the predicate.

v2-l4.source: அன்பொடு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v2-l4.roman: aṉpoṭu nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v2-l4.english: {0:are lovingly}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v2-l4.grammarNote: Sociative noun aṉpoṭu (aṉpu + oṭu) functioning adverbially; reduplicated adjectives nalla nalla; sandhi split aṭiyā + ravarkku.

v2-extra.grammarNote: Refrain phrase: nalla + aṭiyār-avarkku + mikavē. The performance repeats this complete phrase twice.

v3-l1.source: உருவளர் பவளமேனி ஒளிநீறணிந்து உமையோடும் வெள்ளை விடைமேல்
v3-l1.roman: uruvaḷar pavaḷamēṉi oḷinīṟaṇintu umaiyōṭum veḷḷai viṭaimēl
v3-l1.english: {1:His coral body}{0: radiant in form,}{2: smeared with glowing sacred ash,}{3: together with Umā}{4: upon the white}{5: bull,}
v3-l1.grammarNote: uruvaḷar (uru + vaḷar), pavaḷamēṉi (pavaḷam + mēṉi), oḷinīṟaṇintu (oḷi + nīṟu + aṇintu, adverbial participle), umaiyōṭum (sociative with -um), viṭaimēl (viṭai + postposition mēl).

v3-l2.source: முருகலர் கொன்றை திங்கள் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v3-l2.roman: murukalar koṉṟai tiṅkaḷ muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v3-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{0: fragrant blooming}{1: golden shower blossoms}{2: and the crescent moon,}{6: He entered}{4: into my}{5: heart;}{7: therefore,}
v3-l2.grammarNote: murukalar = muruku (fragrance) + alar (blossoming); muṭimēl split across tokens as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ).

v3-l3.source: திருமகள் கலையதூர்தி செயமாது பூமி திசை தெய்வமான பலவும்
v3-l3.roman: tirumakaḷ kalaiyatūrti ceyamātu pūmi ticai teyvamāṉa palavum
v3-l3.english: {0:the Goddess of Fortune,}{1: the stag-mounted}{2: goddess of victory,}{3: the Earth,}{6: and the many}{4,5: directional deities,}

words.gloss: she whose mount is the stag (Durgā)
being deities / the presiding deities of

v3-l3.grammarNote: kalaiyatūrti (stag as vehicle) and ceyamātu (goddess of victory) are read together as two descriptions of Durgā, not two separately introduced goddesses. teyvamāṉa = teyvam + āṉa; palavum is inclusive plural.

v3-l4.source: அருநெதி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v3-l4.roman: aruneti nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v3-l4.english: {0:like precious wealth, are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}

words.gloss: rare, precious wealth; here an image of their benefit

v3-l4.grammarNote: aruneti combines aru (rare, precious) with neti/niti (wealth, treasure), placing the preceding deities in the image of precious wealth. English makes the implied comparison explicit with ‘like’; it does not add a separate boon or another deity to the list. The repeated nalla predicates their goodness; aṭiyā + ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku (for the devotees).

v4-l1.source: மதிநுதன் மங்கையோடு வடாலிருந்து மறையோதும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v4-l1.roman: matinutaṉ maṅkaiyōṭu vaṭāliruntu maṟaiyōtum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v4-l1.english: {4:Our}{5: Supreme Lord who,}{2: seated beneath the banyan tree}{0: with the moon-browed}{1: maiden,}{3: expounds the Vedas,}
v4-l1.grammarNote: matinutaṉ = mati (moon) + nutal (forehead, with euphonic nasalization); vaṭāliruntu = vaṭa (north/banyan) + āl (banyan tree) + iruntu (having stayed/sat); maṟaiyōtum = maṟai + ōtum (relative participle).

v4-l2.source: நதியொடு கொன்றைமாலை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v4-l2.roman: natiyoṭu koṉṟaimālai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v4-l2.english: {3:having adorned}{2: His crown with}{0: the river}{1: and a garland of golden shower blossoms,}{5: entered}{3: into my}{4: heart;}{6: therefore,}
v4-l2.grammarNote: natiyoṭu (nati + oṭu); muṭimēl split across sandhi as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ).

v4-l3.source: கொதியுறு காலன் அங்கி நமனோடு தூதர் கொடுநோய்க ளான பலவும்
v4-l3.roman: kotiyuṟu kālaṉ aṅki namaṉōṭu tūtar koṭunōyka ḷāṉa palavum
v4-l3.english: {0:wrathful}{1: Death,}{2: fire,}{3: Yama along with his}{4: messengers,}{6,7: and all the many}{5: severe afflictions}
v4-l3.grammarNote: kotiyuṟu = koti (boil/rage) + uṟu; namaṉōṭu (namaṉ + oṭu); koṭunōykaḷ split across sandhi as koṭunōyka + ḷāṉa (ḷ + āṉa).

v4-l4.source: அதிகுணம் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v4-l4.roman: atikuṇam nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v4-l4.english: {0:are supremely beneficial,}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v4-l4.grammarNote: atikuṇam = ati (supreme/exceeding) + kuṇam (guṇa / beneficial quality); sandhi split aṭiyā + ravarkku.

v5-l1.source: நஞ்சணி கண்டன் எந்தை மடவாள் தனோடும் விடையேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v5-l1.roman: nañjaṇi kaṇṭaṉ entai maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum viṭaiyēṟum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v5-l1.english: {2:Our Father}{6,7: and Supreme Lord,}{1: whose throat}{0: is adorned with poison,}{5: who mounts the bull}{4: along with}{3: the gentle maiden,}
v5-l1.grammarNote: nañjaṇi = nañju + aṇi; entai = eṉ + tantai (my/our father); maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum (maṭavāḷ + taṉ + oṭu + um); viṭaiyēṟum = viṭai + ēṟum (relative participle).

v5-l2.source: துஞ்சிருள் வன்னி கொன்றை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v5-l2.roman: tuñjiruḷ vaṉṉi koṉṟai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v5-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{0: dark, dense}{1: Indian mesquite}{2: and golden shower blossoms,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: heart;}{7: therefore,}
v5-l2.grammarNote: tuñjiruḷ qualifies the adjacent vaṉṉi with its dense darkness; it does not specify the time of entry into the heart. muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v5-l3.source: வெஞ்சின அவுணரோடும் உருமிடியும் மின்னும் மிகையான பூதமவையும்
v5-l3.roman: veñciṉa avuṇarōṭum urumiṭiyum miṉṉum mikaiyāṉa pūtamavaiyum

words.gloss: those elemental spirits / beings as well

v5-l3.grammarNote: avuṇarōṭum contains associative suffix -ōṭu and connective -um; urumiṭiyum, miṉṉum, and pūtamavaiyum have coordinating conjunctive -um; pūtamavaiyum combines pūtam + avai + um.

v5-l4.source: அஞ்சிடும் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v5-l4.roman: añciṭum nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē

words.gloss: will be filled with dread / will fear

v5-l4.grammarNote: añciṭum is future/habitual 3rd person neuter plural verb; aṭiyā ravarkku represents sandhi split of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); nalla nalla is an aṭukku-t-toṭar (intensive reduplication).

v6-l1.source: வாள்வரி யதளதாடை வரி கோவணத்தர் மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v6-l1.roman: vāḷvari yataḷatāṭai vari kōvaṇattar maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v6-l1.english: {0:Clad in radiant-striped }{1:skin as His garment, }{3:the wearer of a }{2:bound }{3:loincloth, }{6:united together }{5:with }{4:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: skin of that as His garment
the one who wears a loincloth

v6-l1.grammarNote: yataḷatāṭai contains glide y + ataḷatu (skin) + āṭai (garment); kōvaṇattar is a pronominal noun (3rd person honorific masculine); taṉōṭum contains reflexive singular taṉ + associative ōṭu + connective um.

v6-l2.source: நாண்மலர் வன்னி கொன்றை நதிசூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v6-l2.roman: nāṇmalar vaṉṉi koṉṟai naticūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v6-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:fresh blossoms, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:golden shower, }{3:and the river, }{4:came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v6-l2.grammarNote: nāṇmalar is sandhi of nāḷ (fresh/day) + malar (flower); vanteṉ is vantu (verbal participle) + eṉ (oblique 1st person singular 'my'); ataṉāl is instrumental ablative causal connective ('on account of that').

v6-l3.source: கோளரி யுழுவையோடு கொலையானை கேழல் கொடுநாக மோடு கரடி
v6-l3.roman: kōḷari yuḻuvaiyōṭu kolaiyāṉai kēḻal koṭunāka mōṭu karaṭi
v6-l3.english: {0:the predatory lion }{1:along with the tiger, }{2:the murderous elephant, }{3:the wild boar, }{5:along with }{4:the deadly serpent, }{6:and the bear,}
v6-l3.grammarNote: yuḻuvaiyōṭu includes inserted glide y and associative suffix -ōṭu; mōṭu represents sandhi of -m (from koṭunākam) + ōṭu.

v6-l4.source: ஆளரி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v6-l4.roman: āḷari nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v6-l4.grammarNote: aṭiyā ravarkku is the split surface form of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); avai is 3rd person neuter plural pronoun standing for all wild animals.

v7-l1.source: செப்பிள முலைநன்மங்கை ஒருபாக மாக விடையேறு செல்வனடைவார்
v7-l1.roman: ceppiḷa mulaiṉaṉmaṅkai orupāka māka viṭaiyēṟu celvaṉaṭaivār
v7-l1.english: With the {3:noble maiden }of {1:youthful }{0:cup-like }{2:breasts }{6:as }{4:one }{5:half, }{9:the prosperous Lord }{8:who mounts }{7:the bull}{10:—reached by}

words.gloss: reaching or settling upon Him (continuing with the waters in the next line)

v7-l1.grammarNote: The surface celvaṉaṭaivār spans celvaṉ and aṭaivu ār. The latter continues into the following line and describes the waters reaching or settling upon the Lord; it does not introduce devotees as an agent. The cup-like youthful breasts belong to the noble maiden, who is His half.

v7-l2.source: ஒப்பிள மதியும் அப்பும் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v7-l2.roman: oppiḷa matiyum appum muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v7-l2.english: {2:the waters—}{4:wearing them, }with the {0:peerless young }{1:moon, }{3:upon His crown, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v7-l2.grammarNote: oppiḷa = oppu (comparison/equal) + il (without) + a / iḷa (young); muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl (locative 'upon the crown') + aṇintu (adorned) + eṉ (my).

v7-l3.source: வெப்பொடு குளிரும் வாதம் மிகையான பித்தும் வினையான வந்து நலியா
v7-l3.roman: veppoṭu kuḷirum vātam mikaiyāṉa pittum viṉaiyāṉa vantu naliyā
v7-l3.english: {0:fever along with }{1:chills, }{2:wind-humor afflictions, }{3:excessive }{4:bile-humor afflictions, }{5:and distresses born of deeds }{7:will not }{6:come }{7:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: those born of past deeds / karmic distresses
will not afflict; will not cause harm

v7-l3.grammarNote: naliyā is a negative 3rd person neuter plural verb from root nali (to torment/crush); viṉaiyāṉa is an adjectival/pronominal appellative form referring to deeds/consequences.

v7-l4.source: அப்படி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v7-l4.roman: appaṭi nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v7-l4.english: {0:thus they are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v7-l4.grammarNote: appaṭi functions as an adverbial connective of manner ('just so / likewise'); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v8-l1.source: வேள்பட விழிசெய் தன்று விடைமே லிருந்து மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v8-l1.roman: vēḷpaṭa viḻicey taṉṟu viṭaimē liruntu maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v8-l1.english: {1:Having opened His eye }{2:on that day }{0:so that Kāma would perish, }{4:seated }{3:upon the bull }{7:together }{6:with }{5:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: for Kāma (the god of desire) to perish / fall

v8-l1.grammarNote: vēḷpaṭa is an infinitive of purpose/result (vēḷ + paṭa); viḻiceytaṉṟu is split into viḻicey + taṉṟu (ta- inserted before aṉṟu); viṭaimē liruntu is sandhi of viṭaimēl + iruntu.

v8-l2.source: வாண்மதி வன்னி கொன்றை மலர்சூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v8-l2.roman: vāṇmati vaṉṉi koṉṟai malarcūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v8-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:the radiant moon, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:and golden shower }{3:blossoms, }{4:He came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v8-l2.grammarNote: vāṇmati combines vāḷ (bright) + mati (moon); malarcūṭi is compound of malar (flower) + cūṭi (verbal participle 'having worn').

v8-l3.source: ஏழ்கடல் சூழிலங்கை அரையன்த னோடும் இடரான வந்து நலியா
v8-l3.roman: ēḻkaṭal cūḻilaṅkai araiyaṉta ṉōṭum iṭarāṉa vantu naliyā
v8-l3.english: {2:the king }{1:of Laṅkā }{1:surrounded by }{0:seven oceans }{3:along with }{4:all distresses }{6:will not }{5:come }{6:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: will not afflict; will not cause harm

v8-l3.grammarNote: ēḻkaṭal combines ēḻu (seven) + kaṭal (sea); araiyanta ṉōṭum represents araiyan (king) + oblique -ta- + associative -ōṭu + connective -um.

v8-l4.source: ஆழ்கடல் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v8-l4.roman: āḻkaṭal nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v8-l4.grammarNote: āḻkaṭal is a viṉait-tokai compound from āḻ (to sink/be deep) + kaṭal (ocean); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-l1.source: பலபல வேட மாகும் பரனாரி பாகன் பசுவேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v9-l1.roman: palapala vēṭa mākum paraṉāri pākaṉ pacuvēṟum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v9-l1.english: {3:The Supreme One,}{2: assuming}{0: manifold}{1: guises,}{4: having}{3: the woman}{4: as His half,}{6: our}{7: Supreme Lord}{5: who rides the bull,}

words.gloss: the Supreme One; the woman (in nāri-pākaṉ, woman-as-half)
one who has as His half

v9-l1.grammarNote: palapala is intensive reduplication of pala (many); vēṭa mākum combines vēṭam + ākum (relative participle); pacuvēṟum is pacu (bull) + ēṟum (mounting).

v9-l2.source: சலமக ளோடு எருக்கு முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v9-l2.roman: calamaka ḷōṭu erukku muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v9-l2.english: {4:wearing }{3:upon His crown }{0:the daughter of the waters }{1:along with }{2:crown flowers, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v9-l2.grammarNote: calamaka ḷōṭu represents calamakaḷ (calam 'water' + makaḷ 'daughter') + associative suffix -ōṭu; muṭimē laṇinteṉ is sandhi for muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v9-l3.source: மலர்மிசை யோனும் மாலும் மறையோடு தேவர் வருகால மான பலவும்
v9-l3.roman: malarmicai yōṉum mālum maṟaiyōṭu tēvar varukāla māṉa palavum
v9-l3.english: {1:He }{0:upon the lotus }{1:and }{2:Viṣṇu, }{3:along with }{3:the Vedas, }{4:the gods, }{7:and all the manifold things }{6:that constitute }{5:the future,}

words.gloss: Māl, the Great One, Viṣṇu, also
all the manifold entities as well

v9-l3.grammarNote: malarmicai yōṉum is sandhi for malarmicaiyōṉ (pronominal noun: 'he who is on the flower', Brahmā) + -um; mālum has connective -um; varukāla māṉa combines varukālam + āṉa.

v9-l4.source: அலைகடல் மேரு நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-l4.roman: alaikaṭal mēru nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-l4.grammarNote: alaikaṭal is a viṉait-tokai (alai 'surge/wave' + kaṭal 'sea'); aṭiyā ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees, }they are {8:good, }{9:good—}{7:exceedingly so; }{10,11:for His devotees—}{12:exceedingly so!}
v9-extra.grammarNote: Consists of three repeated cycles of the refrain formula aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla.

v10-l1.source: கொத்தலர் குழலி யோடு விசயற்கு நல்கு குணமாய வேட விகிர்தன்
v10-l1.roman: kottalar kuḻali yōṭu vicayaṟku nalku kuṇamāya vēṭa vikirtaṉ
v10-l1.english: {2:Along with }{1:Her of }{0:blossoming flower-cluster }{1:tresses, }{7:the Transcendent Lord of varied forms }who in {5:gracious }{6:hunter }{6:guise }{4:bestowed grace }{3:upon Arjuna,}

words.gloss: the Transcendent Lord of varied forms

v10-l1.grammarNote: kottalar is kottu (cluster) + alar (blossom); kuḻali yōṭu has inserted glide y and associative -ōṭu; vicayaṟku is dative singular of vicayaṉ (Arjuna); vikirtaṉ is derived from Sanskrit vikṛta ('one who assumes varied forms / the Transcendent').

v10-l2.source: மத்தமும் மதியும் நாகம் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v10-l2.roman: mattamum matiyum nākam muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v10-l2.english: {4:wearing}{0: datura,}{1: the crescent moon,}{2: and the serpent}{3: upon His crest,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: very heart;}{7: therefore,}
v10-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi breaks across tokens: `muṭi mēl` + `aṇintu` + `eṉ` yields surface tokens `muṭimē` and `laṇinteṉ`. Relative participle `pukunta` modifies causal instrumental pronoun `ataṉāl`. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v10-l3.source: புத்தரொ டமணை வாதில் அழிவிக்கும் அண்ணல் திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே
v10-l3.roman: puttaro ṭamaṇai vātil aḻivikkum aṇṇal tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē
v10-l3.english: {4:the exalted Lord’s }{5:sacred ash }{3:defeats }{0:Buddhists }{1:and Jains }{2:in debate—}{6:its goodness }{7:is assured; }{8:the sacred ash’s }{9:goodness }{10:is assured; }{11:the sacred ash’s }{12:goodness }{13:is assured.}

words.gloss: causes defeat; here, the sacred ash defeats opponents in debate

v10-l3.grammarNote: Aḻivikkum is a causative relative form attached to the full noun phrase aṇṇal tirunīṟu: the Lord’s sacred ash is the effective subject. Cemmai is its goodness or excellence; tiṭamē affirms that this is assured. The three performed occurrences are retained individually.

v10-l4.source: அத்தகு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-l4.roman: attaku nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-l4.english: {0:Such things are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v10-l4.grammarNote: Reduplication of `nalla` emphasizes absolute auspiciousness. Sandhi split across tokens: `aṭiyār` + `avarkku` -> `aṭiyā` and `ravarkku`.

v10-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees—}{7:exceedingly so; }{8,9:for His devotees—}{10:exceedingly so!}
v10-extra.grammarNote: Liturgical refrain repeating the cadence of the verse's final quarter (`aṭiyāravarkku mikavē`).

v11-l1.source: தேனமர் பொழில்கொள் ஆலை விளைசெந்நெல் துன்னி வளர்செம்பொன் எங்கும் நிகழ
v11-l1.roman: tēṉamar poḻilkoḷ ālai viḷaicennel tuṉṉi vaḷarcempoṉ eṅkum nikaḻa
v11-l1.english: Amid {0:honey-rich }{1:groves, }{2:sugarcane mills, }and {3:ripening red rice }{4:clustered together, }{5:fine gold abounding }{6:everywhere }{7:in sight,}
v11-l1.grammarNote: Infinitive `nikaḻa` functions adverbially/circumstantially ('as ... shines/manifests'). Compound chain: `tēṉ-amar` (honey-settling), `poḻil-koḷ` (grove-bearing), `viḷai-cem-nel` (ripening-red-paddy), `vaḷar-cem-poṉ` (growing-fine-gold).

v11-l2.source: நான்முகன் ஆதி யாய பிரமா புரத்து மறைஞான ஞான முனிவன்
v11-l2.roman: nāṉmukaṉ āti yāya piramā purattu maṟaiñāṉa ñāṉa muṉivaṉ
v11-l2.english: {6:the wise }{7:sage, }{5:versed in Vedic knowledge, }{3,4:of Brahmapuram, }{1,2:which takes its name from }{0:the Four-faced One,}

words.gloss: origin or beginning; here, the origin of the city’s name
being or becoming; linking the origin to Brahmapuram

v11-l2.grammarNote: Nāṉmukaṉ is the Four-faced One. Āti yāya relates the origin of Brahmapuram to him; it does not say that he owns the city. Maṟaiñāṉa gives Vedic knowledge, and ñāṉa qualifies the sage as wise. The English subject is this sage, continued by spoke in the next row.

v11-l3.source: தானுறு கோளும் நாளும் அடியாரை வந்து நலியாத வண்ணம் உரைசெய்
v11-l3.roman: tāṉuṟu kōḷum nāḷum aṭiyārai vantu naliyāta vaṇṇam uraicey
v11-l3.english: {7:spoke }{6:so that }{1:planets }{2:and asterisms, }{0:as they take their course, }{5:may not }{4:come }{5:and afflict }{3:devotees.}

words.gloss: spoke or composed; here, the sage’s utterance that forms the following word-garland

v11-l3.grammarNote: Naliyāta is negative and qualifies vaṇṇam: so that they do not afflict. Uraicey is the utterance/composition expression linked to the following garland of words; do not assert an overt past-tense suffix absent from the supplied form. English uses spoke as a finite clause, then resumes the resulting garland with this in the next sentence.

v11-l4.source: ஆனசொல் மாலை யோதும் அடியார்கள் வானில் அரசாள்வர் ஆணை நமதே
v11-l4.roman: āṉacol mālai yōtum aṭiyārkaḷ vāṉil aracāḷvar āṇai namatē
v11-l4.english: {3:Devotees }{2:who recite }{1:this garland }{0:of potent words }{5:shall reign }{4:in heaven; }{7:this is our }{6:solemn decree!}
v11-l4.grammarNote: Sandhi: `mālai` + `ōtum` -> `mālai yōtum`. Future verb `aracāḷvar` asserts the promised fruit. `āṇai namatē` is an emphatic nominal sentence of sovereign declaration.

v11-closing.grammarNote: Nominal sentence `āṇai namatē` (noun + possessive pronoun with emphatic `-ē`) chanted in fourfold repetition.

featureDispositions.reason: The repeated entered-my-heart clause makes the divine inward presence explicit in each stanza. Correcting dark/dense to qualify vanni removes an unsupported time circumstance, without changing the entry or indwelling.

The hymn repeatedly promises that planets, days, fierce beings, illness and other possible harms will instead act beneficially for the devotees; the final verse explicitly says planets/days will not afflict them.
Repeated epithets praise the poison-throated, bull-riding Lord adorned with moon, river and flowers; the closing calls the hymn a garland of words to recite.

Uma is explicitly named riding with Shiva in v3-l1; repeated descriptions show the lady accompanying him or sharing half his body. This is a narrated companionship role, not merely direct address or an inferred goddess.
The praised Lord bears the consumed poison, crescent and Ganga, rides the bull with Uma, and burns Kama with his gaze. These linked identities establish Shiva as the focus independently of metadata.

lineEvidence.line-018: Parabrahma is the supreme reality manifest as incarnation, an ordinary philosophical concept under the public English contract.

lineEvidence.line-045: The people are deluded by māyā and seek liberation. Render this world-appearance power contextually; this does not reduce every māyā use to bare illusion.

featureDispositions.reason: Sai is called all-pervading and permeating the whole universe.
Grace dispels distress, grants aims and is obtained through devoted recitation.
The text asks liberation from delusion and explicitly describes final liberation.
Those distressed in worldly existence take refuge at the feet; the singer declares no other shelter.
Requests seek repose, relief, removal of sins and forgiveness.
Victory cries and repeated bowing extol Sai and Datta.
Datta Digambara/Avadhūta is explicitly addressed and identified as son of Anasūyā and Atri.
The worshipped addressee is explicitly the true Guru and king of Gurus.
Sāī Bābā/Sāīnātha is repeatedly the explicit worship focus.

featureDispositions.reason: Sustained descriptions contemplate locks, forehead, charming form and ash-adorned body.
The closing calls Śiva compassion embodied, supporting the appeal to gracious protection.
Devotional recitation/listening is said to attain union with Śiva.
Repeated protection requests and removal of threefold suffering establish refuge.
The feet are held in the heart while the worshipper beholds Maheśa.
Protect me always through grace is a direct repeated request.
Victory cries and Śiva’s epithets repeatedly hail the deity.
Gaurī/Girijā appears beside Hara and acts in the described scene, supporting narrative_subject.
Gaṅgādhara, Hara, Girijā’s Lord and Mahādeva explicitly identify the worshipped Śiva.
